question: Who are you, Laari?
answer: I’m Laari, NCRI-Ghana’s virtual guide. I can answer common questions about our work, how to give, volunteer or partner, and where to find things on this website.

question: What is NCRI-Ghana?
answer: NCRI-Ghana (Northern Community Resilience Initiative) is a community-focused initiative based in Saboba, Northern Region, Ghana. We work with communities, especially women, girls and young people, on quality education, livelihoods and resilience to climate and social challenges.

question: Where are you based?
answer: Our head office is in Saboba, Northern Region, Ghana.

question: Is NCRI-Ghana registered?
answer: NCRI-Ghana is currently being established and is not yet registered or licensed. We will announce registration here as soon as it is complete.

question: What is your vision?
answer: A resilient and inclusive Northern Ghana where every child, woman, girl, young person and vulnerable household has the opportunity to live safely, learn, prosper and participate meaningfully in community development.

question: What is your mission?
answer: To empower vulnerable and underserved communities through quality education, child protection, women’s and girls’ empowerment, climate-resilient agriculture, youth development, livelihoods and meaningful community participation.

question: What are your core values?
answer: Integrity and accountability, dignity, inclusion, equality, community ownership, innovation, sustainability, partnership and transparency. You can read what each one means on our About page.

question: Who leads NCRI-Ghana?
answer: Profiles of our board, management, staff, volunteers and interns will appear on the About page once they are published by the team.

question: How do I contact you?
answer: Use the form on the Contact page. Our head office is in Saboba, Northern Region. Official phone and email details will be published after they are verified.

question: How do I get updates?
answer: Subscribe with your email address at the bottom of any page, and follow the News & Updates page for stories from our work.

question: Where can I find reports and toolkits?
answer: The Resources page has reports, toolkits, briefs and training materials that you can search and download for free.

question: Can I watch live events or videos?
answer: Yes. The Live & Videos page shows our live broadcasts when we are streaming and keeps a library of videos.

question: How can I donate?
answer: Open the Donate page and choose a route: Local Partners / Ghana, International, or Online. Payment details are shared only after they have been verified, and every gift is recorded with a reference number.

question: Can I give by mobile money?
answer: The Local Partners / Ghana route is where Ghana-based giving options, such as mobile money or bank transfer, are listed once their details are verified. Please check the Donate page for what is available now.

question: Can I donate from outside Ghana?
answer: Yes. The International route on the Donate page covers bank transfer and online options for supporters abroad, as well as foundation and institutional giving.

question: Is online giving secure?
answer: When online payments are enabled, they are handled by secure payment providers such as Paystack or Stripe. NCRI-Ghana does not see or store your card details.

question: How can I volunteer?
answer: Go to the Get Involved page and fill in the volunteer form with your skills and availability. The team will contact you.

question: How can my organisation partner with you?
answer: We welcome partnerships with communities, government institutions, schools, traditional leaders, civil society, foundations, development partners and responsible businesses. See the Partnerships page and send an enquiry.

question: Where can I read your policies?
answer: Our Policies page lists accountability, anti-fraud and anti-corruption, complaints and whistleblowing, conflict of interest, financial management and procurement. Approved documents can be downloaded there.

question: How do I report a concern or make a complaint?
answer: Please read the Complaints & Whistleblowing section on the Policies page, then send your concern through the Contact page and choose “Complaint / concern”. We take every concern seriously.

question: What programmes do you run?
answer: We work across six pillars: Child Protection & Education; Women & Girls’ Empowerment; Agriculture, Food Security & Rural Livelihoods; Youth Development, Skills & Employment; Climate, Governance & Community Resilience; and Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH). Tap any pillar on the Programmes page for its overview and available stories.

question: Tell me about girls’ education.
answer: Our featured initiative, the Northern Girls’ Education & Protection Initiative, aims to keep girls in school, strengthen child protection, support families and communities, and create safe and inclusive learning environments.

question: Who do you work with and who benefits?
answer: We work with communities, especially women, girls, young people and vulnerable households in Northern Ghana, together with schools, traditional leaders, government institutions and civil society organisations.

question: What are your impact targets?
answer: By 2027 we aim to reach 500–1,000 children and adolescents, 200–300 women and girls, 150–250 farmers and 100–200 young people. These are planning targets, and we report progress on the Monitoring & Learning page.

question: How do you measure results?
answer: Through Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL): we track activities and results against agreed indicators, review what changed and why, and share what we learn with communities and partners.
